draft.title: The external environment
card: The external environment is made up of forces outside a business that it cannot control. Because it cannot change them, a business must respond to them.
broad forces that affect all businesses, such as the economy, laws, government policy, technology and changes in society.
also called the operating environment. It is the customers, suppliers and competitors a business deals with directly, so it differs from one business to the next.
Responding means adapting, such as changing prices, products or plans. An owner cannot stop a new law or a rival opening nearby, but can plan for it.
draft.remember: General forces touch every business. Market forces are its own customers, suppliers and competitors.

a.q: Which of these is part of a café's external environment?
opts: A new law on how food must be labelled
The skills of the café's own staff
The owner's choice of opening hours
The range of meals the café decides to sell
a.why: A new law comes from outside the café and the owner cannot change it, only respond. Staff skills, opening hours and the menu are decisions the business makes itself, so they are not external forces.
a.clue: Which one could the owner not change by making a decision?

b.q: Priya runs a bike shop in Ballarat. A rival bike store opens across the street. How is this best described?
b.why: A competitor is part of the market environment, the customers, suppliers and competitors a business deals with directly. Priya cannot stop it opening, so it is outside her control. It is not the general environment, because a new store in one street does not affect all businesses.
b.clue: Does this rival affect every business, or mainly shops like Priya's?

a.best: A new law on how food must be labelled
